This run at a glance

Generated by otherlivestockops.render-html (kbb -M:render-html) by driving otherlivestockops.operation → advisor → governor → phase → store. Every id, count, cost, disposition and Japanese hold detail below is read back from that run; nothing on this page is typed by hand.

  • 17 operations run across 5 registered holdings plus one unregistered id apiary-999.
  • 7 HARD Governor refusals, covering 5 distinct rules: facility-not-registered, husbandry-count-invalid, no-execution, op-not-allowed, treatment-or-harvest-blocked. None of these reached a human.
  • 4 autonomous commits and 5 escalations queued for a farm operator / veterinarian.
  • 1 rollout phase-gate hold — counted separately from the refusals above, because in this repo the phase gate emits the same :governor-hold fact type with an empty :violations.

8 · Who-acted attribution (measured, not assumed)

Probed at render time by walking every fact and record this run produced at every depth, the otherlivestockops.store/Store protocol's own method set, and a before/after Store snapshot. If this repo later grows an approval path these rows change on their own — nothing here is a hard-coded claim about the scaffold. :actor is reported in its own column and is deliberately excluded from the approver probe: it is bound from (:actor-id context), the executing actor.

What the probe above means

Commits and holds do name the acting actor (:actor other-livestock-ops-01), so the audit trail is not anonymous. But no human approver is recorded anywhere, at any depth, on any fact or record this run produced — and that is a measured drop, not merely an absence: every run in this scenario was handed :approver sato-dvm-01 in its context, and a deep scan by value finds it in none of the emitted facts, none of the returned records, and nowhere in the Store. The reason is structural rather than a single dropped field: otherlivestockops.store/Store exposes 1 read method (registered-facility) and no write method at all — add-facility mutates the MemStore atom directly, outside the protocol — there is no resume/approve entry point in the repo, and the :approval-requested fact has no approver slot to fill.

The Store is identical before and after the run, and the 4 committed record(s) exist only as return values of run-operation — nothing this actor commits is persisted. A reader should not have to guess whether nobody approved or whether the approval was lost: for this build, no approval can be recorded at all, and no commit survives the call that produced it.

Regenerate with kbb -M:render-html. The page contains no timestamps and no per-run identifiers, and is byte-identical across reruns from the same seed. -main refuses to write unless the run produced at least one :governor-hold fact carrying a non-empty :violations vector, at least one commit and at least one escalation — a phase-gate hold with empty violations does not satisfy it.

Known defect, surfaced not patched: otherlivestockops.operation/run-operation derives an escalation's :reason from :high-stakes?, which otherlivestockops.governor/check sets for BOTH an always-escalate op and a cost above threshold. A cost-driven escalation is therefore recorded as :always-escalate. Measured in this run on R04, R06 — see the highlighted derived driver cells in section 5.

Second finding, surfaced not patched: the rollout phase gate's conservative hold for an unrecognised phase is written as a :governor-hold fact, the same type the Governor uses for a real refusal. The two are only separable by the emptiness of :violations (section 4). Any downstream consumer counting fact types alone will over-report refusals.
